observations: Photo 0 shows a yellow industrial diesel engine assembly with multiple hoses/lines and an open/visible cylinder block area; no clear model plate visible.
Photo 1 shows the top/valve cover area of a diesel engine with wiring/hoses; again no clearly readable Caterpillar model/serial plate.
Seller text claims “Complete caterpiller c9 engine (parts)” and “Tested and working, no knock, low mileage, never opened,” but photos do not show proof of testing or mileage.

claims.evidence: Photos show a diesel engine assembly, but no readable Caterpillar C9 identification plate/label and no clear confirmation it is complete vs partial/parts.
No shipping/import documents or markings visible in photos to confirm origin.
No video/scan/test sheet showing running condition, fault codes, or compression/leak test.
No audio/video of engine running or mechanic test report.
No odometer/ECU hours/engine serial data visible in photos.
Photos do not show tamper evidence (seal marks, bolt condition) clearly enough to confirm never opened.

risks.risk: Model mismatch: the engine may not be Caterpillar C9 (photos don’t show a readable model/serial plate). This affects compatibility and price.
risks.proof: A clear close-up photo of the Caterpillar data plate/engine serial/model stamping (and/or ECU/engine tag) plus the full engine serial number.
risks.if_unproven: Price as a generic used diesel engine/unknown Caterpillar variant (worst case for matching).

risks.risk: Not truly complete: seller says “complete… (parts)” which can mean missing components (turbo, injectors, alternator, wiring harness, sensors, flywheel/housing).
risks.proof: A photo checklist laid out: turbo, starter, alternator, fuel pump/injectors, intake/exhaust manifolds, sensors, wiring harness, oil pan, timing components, and any included accessories—showing what is present.

risks.risk: “Tested and working / no knock” may be untrue; engine could have internal wear or hidden faults.
risks.proof: Short video of cold start and idle (with sound), plus a scan tool screenshot showing no active fault codes (or test sheet).
risks.if_unproven: Price as not proven working (worst case: treat as not working until proven).

risks.risk: Damage during removal/transport (bent lines, cracked housings, missing fittings) not obvious from two angles.
risks.proof: Close-ups of all ports/connection points (fuel inlet/outlet, coolant ports, oil drain, sensor ports) and any visible cracks/repairs.
risks.if_unproven: Price with allowance for possible missing/broken fittings (worst case).

proof_requests: Clear close-up of the Caterpillar data plate showing model (C9) and serial number (photo must be readable).
Video of the engine running (cold start if possible) showing idle and no abnormal knocking sound.
Scan tool screenshot showing engine fault codes (or a test sheet) and confirmation of hours/mileage source.
Photos of a full parts inventory to confirm it is complete (turbo, injectors, starter, alternator, sensors, wiring harness, manifolds, and any accessories).
response.reason: The photos show a diesel engine assembly, but the key pricing driver—exact Caterpillar C9 identification and whether it is complete and truly tested—cannot be confirmed from the images provided. Without readable model/serial and proof of working condition, a confident price pick would be unreliable.
